title: Private upgrades: add dashboards + alerting for upgrade execution (steps/failures/rollback/per-customer)
author: Aisha Bello
body: Title: Private upgrades: add dashboards + alerting for upgrade execution (steps/failures/rollback/per-customer) Summary: Adds a small, focused set of Grafana dashboards + Prometheus alert rules to make Private upgrade/rollback runs observable end-to-end. This is intended to be the default SRE/Support view during beta and GA readiness checks. It relies on the structured metrics/logs emitted by the installer + upgrade controller work (ENG-2321) and is referenced by the GA readiness checklist (ENG-2323). Motivation / context: During the first full rehearsal we had to hop between pod logs, ad-hoc PromQL, and k8s events to answer basic questions: which step is stuck, how long have we been in it, are we in rollback, and is it affecting multiple customers/environments. This PR standardizes: 1) a run-level view (status + step timeline), 2) per-step latency distributions, 3) failure/rollback counters + burn-rate style alerts, 4) per-customer status panels for Support. Dashboards added (Grafana): 1) "Private Upgrade / Rollback - Overview" (dashboards/private_upgrade_overview.jsonnet) - Key KPIs: total runs (last 24h/7d), success/failure rate, rollback trigger rate - Panels: current active runs table (by customer_id, environment, target_version, correlation_id), last failed run details (links to logs) - Top failing steps (by step_name) and top error reasons (parsed from labels where present) 2) "Private Upgrade - Step Latency" (dashboards/private_upgrade_step_latency.jsonnet) - p50/p90/p99 step duration by step_name (histogram) - "stuck" detection panels: time since step start for active runs - Filters: region, install_type (vpc/onprem), customer_tier, target_version 3) "Private Upgrade - Customer Status" (dashboards/private_upgrade_customer_status.jsonnet) - Per-customer table: last run status, last run started_at, last known good version, current target version, rollback_safe boolean (from metrics label if present; falls back to unknown) - Intended for Support/PS: quick lookup during escalations to see if multiple customers are impacted by a release 4) "Private Upgrade - Rollback" (dashboards/private_upgrade_rollback.jsonnet) - Rollback triggers over time, rollback reason breakdown, restore duration, and post-rollback health gate outcome - Explicit panels to help answer: did rollback complete and did health gates pass afterward? Alerts added (PrometheusRule): Note: these are intentionally conservative for beta to avoid noise; all alerts are scoped to private deployments and keyed by install_type + customer_id where possible. A) Upgrade run failure spike - Alert: PrivateUpgradeRunFailuresHigh - Expression: increase(redwood_private_upgrade_run_failures_total[30m]) > 0 AND increase(redwood_private_upgrade_run_total[30m]) > 0 - Severity: page (only when failures are non-zero; we can tune to ratio once we have volume) - Annotation includes: correlation_id link template and recommended next action: "collect diagnostics bundle" B) Rollback triggered - Alert: PrivateUpgradeRollbackTriggered - Expression: increase(redwood_private_upgrade_rollback_trigger_total[10m]) > 0 - Severity: page (beta) / ticket (GA candidate; will revisit) - Rationale: rollback triggers are actionable and should be reviewed even if customer impact is mitigated C) Step duration anomaly (p99 regression) - Alert: PrivateUpgradeStepDurationP99High - Expression: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, step_name, install_type) (rate(redwood_private_upgrade_step_duration_seconds_bucket[15m]))) > 900 - Severity: ticket - Notes: this is not per-customer to avoid cardinality; it’s intended to surface step regressions across the fleet after a release D) Upgrade stuck (active run with no step progress) - Alert: PrivateUpgradeRunStuck - Expression: max by (customer_id, correlation_id, install_type) (time() - redwood_private_upgrade_active_step_started_at_seconds) > 1200 - Severity: page (beta) - Caveat: this assumes active_step_started_at_seconds is exported; if not present, this alert will be inert (rule included but gated behind a recording rule that returns NaN when missing) E) Exporter/metrics missing (guardrail) - Alert: PrivateUpgradeMetricsMissing - Expression: absent(up{job="private-upgrade-controller"} == 1) - Severity: ticket - Rationale: dashboards look blank without this; we want a clear signal rather than silent failure Metric assumptions / naming: This PR assumes the following metrics exist (or will exist as part of ENG-2321); all queries are written to degrade gracefully where possible: - redwood_private_upgrade_run_total{status="success|failure", install_type, customer_id?, target_version} - redwood_private_upgrade_run_failures_total{reason?, install_type} - redwood_private_upgrade_step_duration_seconds_bucket{step_name, install_type} - redwood_private_upgrade_rollback_trigger_total{reason?, install_type} - redwood_private_upgrade_active_step_started_at_seconds{customer_id, correlation_id, install_type} (gauge) - redwood_private_upgrade_correlation_info{customer_id, correlation_id, target_version, from_version, install_type} (info) Note on label cardinality: customer_id/correlation_id are only used in table panels and a single "stuck" alert; histograms and fleet-wide alerts aggregate without customer_id to keep series count under control. Files / structure: - dashboards/private_upgrade_overview.jsonnet - dashboards/private_upgrade_step_latency.jsonnet - dashboards/private_upgrade_customer_status.jsonnet - dashboards/private_upgrade_rollback.jsonnet - alerts/private_upgrade.rules.yaml - alerts/recording/private_upgrade.recording.rules.yaml - docs/runbooks/private_upgrade_observability.md (how to use dashboards during upgrade + what to screenshot for Support) - grafana/README.md updates for import + folder conventions Screenshots: - Overview dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/priv-upgrade-overview (internal) - Step latency dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/priv-upgrade-step-latency (internal) - Customer status dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/priv-upgrade-customer-status (internal) How to test: - Local: `make jsonnet-lint` and `make dashboards-render` - Deploy to staging: apply the PrometheusRule + import dashboards via grafana sidecar; then run an upgrade rehearsal in staging and verify: (1) run appears in Active Runs, (2) step durations populate, (3) rollback trigger increments when forcing failure injection. Checklist: - [x] Dashboards render and validate via jsonnet CI - [x] Alert rules pass promtool check - [x] Queries reviewed for cardinality risks - [x] Runbook note added for on-call/Support handoff - [ ] Post-beta: tune thresholds + switch some pages to ticket based on observed volume Review notes / open questions: - We currently use 15m windows for latency; Sean requested 30m windows for low-volume environments (I kept 15m but can adjust). - The stuck alert depends on active_step_started_at_seconds; if installer exports only "step_elapsed" instead, we should align. I included a recording rule stub that handles missing series to avoid broken dashboards/alerts. Related: - Linear: ENG-2321 (upgrade telemetry), ENG-2323 (GA readiness) - Slack thread: eng-sre/thread_1739705012 (initial thresholds + noise concerns) - Incident tagging: incident-bot PR_88 will help auto-link diagnostics; this PR’s runbook points to that flow. Commits: 1) dashboards: add private upgrade overview + step latency 2) dashboards: add per-customer status + rollback views 3) alerts: add private-upgrade alert rules + recording rules 4) docs: add private upgrade observability usage note Review conversation (highlights): - Allison Grant: "Please add a short note in the runbook about which panels are safe to screenshot for customers (avoid internal labels). Also: prefer folder 'Private Deployments' for these dashboards." -> Aisha Bello: "Added docs/runbooks/private_upgrade_observability.md and moved dashboards into the Private Deployments folder in grafana config." - Sean Gallagher: "Cardinality: avoid customer_id in histograms; OK for tables. Can we make rollback triggered page only during beta?" -> Aisha Bello: "Confirmed: histograms aggregate without customer_id. For rollback alert severity, set to page for beta; added TODO for GA to revisit." - Jacob Stein: "Support wants a single table that shows correlation_id + a link to diagnostics bundle location. Can we add a panel that builds the link template?" -> Aisha Bello: "Added a table column 'Diagnostics link' using the standard template. It will work once the installer emits diagnostics_path label; otherwise column shows '-'" CI / checks: - jsonnet-lint: PASS - dashboards-render: PASS - promtool-check: PASS - unit: PASS Merge outcome: Squash merged to main by Allison Grant on 2025-01-22. Release notes: Adds new Private upgrade observability dashboards and alert rules to the observability pack (no customer-facing change; internal ops tooling).
